caption.youtube_title: Five goals at once = zero progress #Shorts

spoken: [hook] Five goals at once usually means zero progress. || Think about it. With work and everything else, you've got maybe five or six free hours a week. Split that five ways, and each goal gets about an hour. That's not enough to move any of them. || [turn] So pick one main goal for the next twelve weeks. Just one. || Say it's launching a side business. That goal gets your five best hours every week. Not whatever leftover time you have at the end of the day. || The other goals don't disappear. They go on the minimum, just enough to keep them alive. || So if you're a runner, you're not training for a race right now. You do two easy runs a week, and you keep your fitness. || And anything you can't even do the minimum for, park it on a list with a date, like January first, when you'll look at it again. || [land] Because one goal that's actually moving beats five goals that are all stuck. || [outro] That's what Dmyor is for. You archive your dream today, so you can see it tomorrow, and break it down into small steps you can actually do. || [outro] If you want to try it out, I've put the link in the bio.
